stories.title: Hosepipe ban extended nationwide from Friday
stories.summary: Uisce Éireann is extending its hosepipe ban nationwide, bringing every county under water restrictions from just after midnight on Friday morning. It comes as Ireland's prolonged spell of hot, dry weather continues to put drinking water supplies under pressure. The six-week Water Conservation Order, which was introduced last week for the Greater Dublin Area and parts of Wexford, Wicklow, Meath, Kildare and south Tipperary, will now apply across the country until 26 August. It is one of the most extensive water conservation measures introduced by Uisce Éireann, with restrictions now applying nationwide as water sources come under increasing strain following an extended period of exceptionally warm and dry weather.

stories.title: Man, 30s, due to appear in court over Waterford stabbing
stories.summary: A man has been charged after a woman was stabbed at a church in Tramore, Co Waterford yesterday morning. The woman in her 50s was seriously injured during the incident at Holy Cross Church in Summerhill before 10am yesterday. She was taken to University Hospital Waterford with serious, but non-life-threatening injuries. The man, who is in his 30s, is due to appear before Waterford District Court later this morning.

stories.title: Government set to publish Summer Economic Statement
stories.summary: The Government will publish details of the Summer Economic Statement later today, which will set out how much money the Coalition will have for tax cuts in the Budget in October. It is expected the room for taxation measures will be in the region of €1.5 billion. This will be on top of capital and current spending increases of about €7bn. The Coalition did not increase the point people pay the higher rate of tax this year.

stories.title: RTÉ's annual report for 2025 to be discussed at Cabinet
stories.summary: The report is due to be discussed by ministers at Government Buildings later this morning, before a likely publication early this afternoon. The annual report for 2025 will outline the financial circumstances at the broadcaster at the end of last year, with attention likely to be placed on issues such as spending levels, voluntary redundancy scheme costs and the TV licence. Positive aspects around what is happening at the organisation are also expected to be outlined. However, significant attention is likely to be placed on the salaries provided to the most senior presenters and managers at the broadcaster - an issue which has repeatedly drawn attention in recent years.

stories.title: Woman arrested by gardaí investigating UCD deception
stories.summary: A woman has been arrested by gardaí investigating alleged deception against a third-level institution. The woman, who is in her 20s, is being detained under Section 4 of the Criminal Justice Act at a south Dublin garda station and can be questioned for up to 24 hours. Gardaí also carried out a search and seized a number of items including electronic devices as part of their investigation. It is understood she is being questioned in relation to allegedly fraudulent documentation supplied to UCD.

stories.title: Legal aid solicitors to begin two-day work stoppage
stories.summary: Solicitors working in the criminal legal aid system in Dublin are expected to begin a two-day work stoppage today in an escalation of the dispute over a new payment scheme which came into effect at the start of the month. The solicitors are calling on the Minister for Justice to engage with them. A further three-day stoppage is planned for next week. There is currently little sign of a resolution to the dispute over the new payment scheme for legal aid solicitors. The dispute arose after a system of paying per court appearance was replaced by a fee of €520 per client.

stories.title: Proposal for municipal councils to be considered
stories.summary: The Government is moving to set up municipal councils around the country, over a decade after town councils were abolished. The Cabinet will consider the proposal today, which has been recommended by the report of a local democracy taskforce set up by Minister of State with responsibility for Local Government and Planning John Cummins and Minister for Housing James Browne. The taskforce has recommended the creation of municipal councils in every local authority, with enhanced budgetary and decision-making powers. In 2014, Ireland's 80 town councils were abolished by then minister Phil Hogan, which dramatically reduced the number of councillors and shifted financial decision-making to county councils.

stories.title: Rebel Wilson wins defamation case in Australia
stories.summary: Australian actor and filmmaker Rebel Wilson has been cleared in a defamation case brought by the lead actress in her directorial debut, The Deb. A Sydney court ruled on Wednesday that Wilson's Instagram posts about Charlotte MacInnes were not defamatory. The dispute centred on an incident in September 2023 when MacInnes and one of the film’s producers went swimming at Sydney’s Bondi Beach and subsequently bathed together. Wilson later posted on Instagram that MacInnes had complained to her about feeling uncomfortable during the incident but had subsequently changed her account.
